title: Powers of Hybrid Numbers: A Unified Algebraic and Combinatorial Framework
content: This paper investigates the algebraic and combinatorial structures governing the exponentiation of generalized hybrid numbers, a non-commutative ring that unifies complex, hyperbolic, and dual number systems. Hybrid rings arise naturally when extending sequences, such as Fibonacci-type or Leonardo-type numbers, into algebraic structures with multiple components. Özdemir's foundational work allows the powers of a hybrid number to be computed by repeated multiplication, through the matrix representation, or in polar form by a De Moivre formula that requires a case distinction according to the type of the number and the computation of a polar angle; to our knowledge, a unified algebraic treatment of arbitrary integer powers, valid for every hybrid number, has not been given. The present paper fills this gap. We show that every hybrid number satisfies a quadratic characteristic equation (unique whenever its vector part is non-zero) determined by its real trace and hybrid character. This foundational property establishes a surjective, non-injective mapping between hybrid numbers and classical second-order linear recurrence sequences, specifically defining the fundamental and fundamental-Lucas characteristic sequences. The study formalizes the anti-involutive property of the hybrid conjugate and provides structural proofs for the multiplicative character identity across all positive, negative, and degenerate integer powers. The core contribution of this work is a unified master theorem establishing four mathematically equivalent frameworks that evaluate every integer power of an arbitrary hybrid number (elliptic, hyperbolic, parabolic or lightlike, with negative powers whenever the number is invertible) without any polar angles: a sequential recursive framework, a decoupled Lucas-equivalence formulation, an analytic structural root expansion utilizing generalized Binet formulas, and a purely real combinatorial expansion that avoids complex arithmetic. Finally, these frameworks are extended to the non-commutative mixed products of arbitrary hybrid powers, providing exact, closed-form combinatorial identities for both positive and negative exponent combinations. We also extend these frameworks to hybrid numbers with complex coefficients, i.e., to the 8-dimensional bi-hybrid algebra C⊗K, and show that identifying the complex unit with the hybrid unit i yields a linear but non-multiplicative collapse onto K. This paper is Part I of a series: Part II extends the theory to hybrid numbers over an arbitrary commutative ring, in particular to hybrid functions, and Part III develops their differential calculus.
